mechanisms.label: Habitat continuity for birds recorded nearby
mechanisms.input: Forest class and canopy on the parcel. Bird records in the 1 km neighbourhood.
mechanisms.hypothesis: The parcel supports breeding or movement of birds that also use neighbouring land.
mechanisms.recipient: Neighbouring land managers and anyone who reports on habitat outcomes.
mechanisms.supporting: 45 neighbourhood records in 26 name groups. Zero parcel records.
mechanisms.alternative: Records cluster where observers walk. The parcel may add nothing that adjacent forest does not.
mechanisms.adverse: A parcel that links habitat can also carry disturbance, pests or fire between the same places.

mrv.question: Which bird species use the parcel in the breeding season, and does the vegetation on the ground match the mapped forest class and canopy?
mrv.support: Exact parcel, 4.235 ha. Two survey stations about 250 m apart along the long axis.
mrv.indicator: Species detected per visit with distance band, and canopy cover per station in percent.
mrv.method: Ten-minute dawn point counts at each station with recorded observer, start time and weather. Record each detection as inside or outside the boundary. One vegetation plot per station with densiometer canopy readings and dominant species.
mrv.timing: Three visits at least seven days apart in the breeding season, dates set by the surveyor.
mrv.role: Field ornithologist engaged by the land steward
mrv.access: Written permission from the verified owner or manager. Ownership is unverified, so confirm it and any permit requirement before entry.
mrv.decision: Keep, narrow or reject the parcel as a candidate for a habitat mechanism.

mechanisms.label: Soil life and the productivity of the land
mechanisms.kind: Framework hypothesis grounded in general soil ecology, untested here
mechanisms.input: Forest cover on the parcel. No soil data.
mechanisms.hypothesis: An intact soil microbial community sustains nutrient cycling and infiltration that neighbouring land and water also draw on.
mechanisms.recipient: The land steward first, then downslope land and water users. None is identified.
mechanisms.supporting: General soil ecology only. No core, sequence or soil chemistry exists for this parcel.
mechanisms.alternative: Soil here may resemble the surrounding forest closely enough that the parcel adds nothing distinctive.
mechanisms.adverse: Soil can also harbour pathogens and store contaminants that move with eroded sediment.

mrv.question: Which bacterial and fungal communities live in the parcel soil, and how do carbon, pH and texture vary along it?
mrv.support: Exact parcel. Five stations along the long axis.
mrv.indicator: Community composition from DNA metabarcoding, with organic carbon in percent, pH and texture class per station.
mrv.method: Composite cores from the top 10 cm at each station, kept cold, with field blanks. Bacterial 16S and fungal ITS metabarcoding at an accredited laboratory, plus standard soil chemistry on the same cores.
mrv.timing: One visit after snowmelt and one in late summer, dates set by the sampler.
mrv.role: Soil ecologist engaged by the land steward
mrv.access: Written permission from the verified owner or manager. Confirm whether a research or collection permit applies on federal land.
mrv.decision: Whether soil function belongs in the candidate file as a measured baseline.

mechanisms.label: Pollinator habitat and pollination nearby
mechanisms.input: Forest edge and mapped shrub cover on the parcel. No pollinator records.
mechanisms.hypothesis: The parcel provides nesting or forage that supports pollinators which also visit flowering plants beyond its boundary.
mechanisms.recipient: Neighbouring land managers, gardeners or growers within flight range. None is identified.
mechanisms.supporting: None locally. No pollinator has been recorded in the reviewed public record.
mechanisms.alternative: Closed conifer canopy may offer little forage, with pollinators concentrated in nearby meadows instead.
mechanisms.adverse: Habitat that shelters pollinators can also shelter pests and their hosts.

mrv.question: Which pollinators use the parcel during bloom, and which flowering plants do they visit?
mrv.support: Exact parcel. One fixed transect along the long axis with three trap stations.
mrv.indicator: Visitors recorded per transect walk by taxon, with the flowering plant visited.
mrv.method: Timed netting along the transect in fair weather and pan traps at three stations, identified to genus or species by a specialist. Record flowering plants in bloom on each visit.
mrv.timing: Three visits across the local bloom period, dates set by the surveyor.
mrv.role: Pollinator ecologist engaged by the land steward
mrv.access: Written permission from the verified owner or manager. Confirm whether a collection permit applies on federal land.
mrv.decision: Keep or drop a pollination mechanism for this parcel.

mechanisms.label: A stepping stone in a habitat network
mechanisms.kind: Framework hypothesis grounded in connectivity science, untested here
mechanisms.input: A forested parcel above the Eagle River. The surrounding habitat network is unmapped.
mechanisms.hypothesis: The parcel links larger habitat patches, so its loss would cut routes that animals, seeds and pollen use to move between them.
mechanisms.recipient: Wildlife managers, neighbouring land stewards and anyone who depends on pollination or game populations nearby. None is identified.
mechanisms.supporting: General evidence only. Corridors raised movement between patches by about 50% across 78 experiments, and stepping stones sustain long-distance dispersal in network models.
mechanisms.alternative: The forest around the parcel may be continuous, in which case the parcel is one tile of a larger floor and its loss changes little.
mechanisms.adverse: A link that carries wildlife can also carry fire, pests and invasive species between the same patches.

mrv.question: Is the parcel a bridge between otherwise separate habitat patches, and do animals use it to cross?
mrv.support: The parcel and the surrounding landscape to at least 5 km.
mrv.indicator: Change in landscape connectivity when the parcel is removed from a mapped habitat network, plus detections per camera-trap night on the parcel.
mrv.method: Map habitat patches from current land-cover data and run a connectivity analysis with and without the parcel. Place two camera traps on the parcel to record crossing animals.
mrv.timing: Desk analysis first, then cameras for one full season, dates set by the analyst.
mrv.role: Landscape ecologist engaged by the land steward
mrv.access: Written permission from the verified owner or manager for camera placement. Confirm any permit on federal land.
mrv.decision: Whether the candidate file should treat the parcel as a connectivity asset.

mechanisms.label: Sediment retention and turbidity downstream
mechanisms.input: Forest cover and zero mapped impervious surface on the parcel.
mechanisms.hypothesis: Vegetated ground on the parcel limits sediment reaching a channel during rain or snowmelt.
mechanisms.recipient: A downstream water user or treatment operator. None is identified.
mechanisms.supporting: Mapped structure only. No runoff, sediment or turbidity has been measured at Eagle.
mechanisms.alternative: The parcel may not drain to a channel that matters, or its contribution may be too small to detect.
mechanisms.adverse: Retained sediment and fuel could accumulate and be released together by a later fire or storm.

mrv.question: Does runoff from the parcel reach a channel, and is turbidity different above and below that point during rain?
mrv.support: The parcel and the nearest receiving channel, located on a site walk.
mrv.indicator: Turbidity in FNU above and below the confluence, with rainfall depth for each event.
mrv.method: Site walk to trace drainage. Then paired grab samples or loggers above and below, read with a calibrated turbidimeter.
mrv.timing: Snowmelt and at least three summer rain events in one season.
mrv.role: Hydrologic technician engaged by the water manager
mrv.access: Written permission for the parcel and both sampling points. Ownership is unverified.
mrv.decision: Continue to a monitored season, or drop the water mechanism for this parcel.

mechanisms.label: Shading and stream temperature
mechanisms.input: Mean canopy cover on the parcel.
mechanisms.hypothesis: Canopy near water lowers peak summer water temperature for a reach below the parcel.
mechanisms.recipient: A fishery manager or water user sensitive to summer temperature. None is identified.
mechanisms.supporting: Canopy is mapped. Temperature in this release is measured only at three separate stations, none placed for this parcel.
mechanisms.alternative: The parcel may not border water. Reach temperature may be set upstream.
mechanisms.adverse: Dense canopy near water can raise fuel continuity along the same corridor.

mrv.question: Is there surface water that the parcel shades, and how does its summer temperature compare above and below?
mrv.support: Any channel within or beside the parcel, confirmed on a site walk.
mrv.indicator: Water temperature in °C at a fixed interval, with daily maximum and coverage per day.
mrv.method: Two calibrated loggers above and below the shaded reach, with the coverage rule used for the station record.
mrv.role: Aquatic technician engaged by the land steward
mrv.access: Written permission for the parcel and logger sites. Ownership is unverified.
mrv.decision: Keep or drop a thermal mechanism before any biological threshold is discussed.

mechanisms.label: Fuel continuity and fire transmission
mechanisms.kind: Framework hypothesis, risk side, untested in Colorado
mechanisms.input: Continuous forest class across the parcel.
mechanisms.hypothesis: Fuel on the parcel connects fire behaviour between neighbouring stands.
mechanisms.recipient: Neighbouring owners and the fire manager. None has been consulted.
mechanisms.supporting: Land-cover class only. No fuel model, canopy base height or fire history for the parcel is in the release.
mechanisms.alternative: Topography and weather may dominate. The parcel is narrow.
mechanisms.adverse: Fuel reduction removes canopy and habitat that the other mechanisms rely on.

mrv.question: What surface and ladder fuels are present, and do they connect to adjacent stands?
mrv.support: Exact parcel and a 100 m strip around it.
mrv.indicator: Fuel load by size class, canopy base height in metres and stand continuity at the boundary.
mrv.method: Standard fuel transects and photo points by a qualified forester. Record the habitat features any treatment would remove.
mrv.timing: One visit after snowmelt and before peak fire season.
mrv.role: Forester engaged by the land steward
mrv.access: Written permission from the verified owner or manager. Any treatment needs separate authority.
mrv.decision: Whether a fuel assessment belongs in the candidate file, with its habitat cost stated.

Taxonomy and issue fields are provider reported. Synonym, fuzzy-match and missing-concept flags remain visible; no current accepted taxonomy is independently asserted.
Neighborhood records do not establish observations on the exact parcel, functional guilds, a mechanism, recipient benefit or financial value.
